selected.selection_reason: Addresses concurrent state mutation through transactional row-lock discipline, with explicit race-oriented integration fixtures.
selected.review_method: Inspected the exact final merge-commit production and regression-test patches. Test evidence is from committed fixtures, without a fresh execution.

Supersedes #1140, #1141, #1142, #1143, #1144, #1145 and #1146 by @Afloat16. Each one edits `docs/ROADMAP.md` and `docs/STATUS.md`, so merging them one at a time would have left each later one in conflict. They're merged together here with the author's commits kept.

- #1140: inline source-map data URLs ignore their fragment, and the scheme and `base64` marker are matched case-insensitively.
- #1141: ZIP directories are recognised from DOS and Unix attributes even without a trailing slash.
- #1142: rejected ASAR names count toward the listing limit.
- #1143: a HAR with a UTF-8 BOM parses.
- #1144: a .NET bundle member can't read into the manifest's bytes.
- #1145: Play can start a Python project's one installed `[project.scripts]` console script from its own environment.
- #1146: Godot and Electron get an absolute project path.

Two fixes on top of the merge:
- #1145 and #1146 each edited the New-project toolchains row in STATUS. It's now one row carrying both additions, not two copies.
- #1146's `launch_tests` module is moved to the end of `outputs.rs`. On Windows an item after it made clippy fail with `items_after_test_module`, which the Linux gate doesn't compile.

**Verified:** the `formats` and `engine` tests (552 in the engine library), clippy for both on Windows, fmt, `cargo xtask wasm` and layers pass on the merged result.

reviewed_pull_requests.title: Space an API backend's requests out with requests_per_minute (R5.4)
reviewed_pull_requests.body:
Refs #668.

## What it does

A service that limits requests per second or minute can now be given that limit, and Craft Anything waits between requests to stay inside it:

```toml
[[ai.backends]]
name = "My provider"
kind = "openai_compatible"
model = "some-model"
requests_per_minute = 120   # two a second
```

Omitted or zero keeps today's behaviour. Until now the app only reacted: it waited and retried after the service had already answered "rate limited", at most three times per turn.

## How

- `BackendOptions::requests_per_minute` (`crates/ai/src/config.rs`), set in `config.toml` like `context_tokens` and `max_turns`.
- `crates/ai/src/pace.rs`: `Paced`, a `ChatModel` wrapper added in `AiHub::slot`. Each request takes the backend's next free time and books the one after it, in one table for the process keyed by backend name. So a crew's workers, or a build and a chat, on the same backend share one limit.
- The wait is polled every 100 ms against `Stop`, so Stop and Pause aren't held by it; the wrapped model then answers the stop as it already does.

## Verified

On Windows 11: `cargo test -p craft-anything-ai` (517 passed, 1 ignored), clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `locks`, `secrets`, `cargo fmt --all --check`. New tests: the rate-to-gap arithmetic, three requests to one backend spaced apart while another backend doesn't wait, a stop ending a 60 s wait, and the setting's round trip through `config.toml`.

## Not done

- No live provider was used.
- `config.toml` only: no control in Settings → AI, and the feed doesn't say when a build is waiting for its turn (roadmap line added for both).
- Requests only. The issue also mentions tokens per second; that needs token counts before sending and is left out.
- Coding-agent apps (Claude Code, Codex…) send their own requests and aren't paced.
- A stopped request keeps the slot it booked, so the next one waits one extra gap.

This adds a setting on a backlog request no maintainer has commented on. If you'd rather shape it differently (another unit, a Settings control first), say so and I'll change or close it.

reviewed_pull_requests.title: Find a Unity Editor added to Unity Hub with Locate (R1.6)
reviewed_pull_requests.body:
Refs #1077 (its second half: "Unity Editor not detected"; the download 404 was fixed in #1078).

## What was wrong

Craft Anything looked for Unity Editors only in Unity Hub's default folders and in the Hub's "install location" setting. An editor added to the Hub with **Locate** can be anywhere, and the Hub records it only in its own list of editors, which we never read. So Make kept saying Unity isn't installed.

## What changed

`unity_editors` (`crates/engines/src/game.rs`) now also reads the Hub's list (`editors-v2.json`, then `editors.json`) and offers every entry whose program is still there.

- The list's layout differs between Hub versions (entries keyed by version, or an array under `data`; `location` a string or an array), so it takes any entry with a `version` and a `location`, to a depth of 4.
- Read is capped at 1 MiB; a list that doesn't parse, a relative path, or an editor that has since been removed finds nothing.
- The Hub's folder is now also looked for under the home folder on macOS (`Library/Application Support/UnityHub`) and Linux (`.config/UnityHub`), for the list and for the existing install-location setting.

## Verified

On Windows 11: `cargo test -p craft-anything-engines` (127 passed, 1 ignored), clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `locks`, `secrets`, `cargo fmt --all --check`. One new test covers both layouts, a removed editor, a relative path and unreadable lists.

## Not verified

- No Unity Hub on the machine this was written on: the list's layout comes from descriptions of it, not from a real file. A roadmap line asks for that check. If a reporter's `editors-v2.json` looks different, please paste it (paths removed).
- Not run on macOS or Linux.
- The reporter may have a different cause (they don't say the editor was added with Locate), so this doesn't close the issue.

A comment on #1077 mentions a fix that reads this file; I found no PR, branch or roadmap claim for it. If one is on its way, close this one.

**Roadmap item:** R3.12, the new line "Swift subscript accessors print the accessor after `subscript` and the type after a colon…". It is claimed in its own commit and ticked in the fix.

**What changed:**

A Swift subscript has accessors like a variable: a getter, a setter, `read` and `modify` coroutines, and unsafe addressors. `swift-demangle` prints one the way it prints a variable's accessor: the accessor name right after `subscript`, then a colon and the subscript's type, as in `Swift.Array.subscript.getter : (Swift.Int) -> A`. `swift_demangle` wrote the type first and the accessor last, `Swift.Array.subscript(Swift.Int) -> A.getter`, so the accessor read as if it belonged to the result type. That was so in every symbol that names a subscript accessor, including dispatch thunks, method descriptors, protocol witnesses and `.resume.0` coroutine parts.

Some symbols from macOS 15.7 and Xcode 26 system binaries:

| Symbol | `swift-demangle` | `main` | here |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_$s10Foundation4DataV06InlineB0Vys5UInt8VSiciM` | `Foundation.Data.InlineData.subscript.modify : (Swift.Int) -> Swift.UInt8` | `Foundation.Data.InlineData.subscript(Swift.Int) -> Swift.UInt8.modify` | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$sSpyxSiciau` | `Swift.UnsafeMutablePointer.subscript.unsafeMutableAddressor : (Swift.Int) -> A` | `Swift.UnsafeMutablePointer.subscript(Swift.Int) -> A.unsafeMutableAddressor` | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$sSly7ElementQz5IndexQzcirTq` | `method descriptor for Swift.Collection.subscript.read : (A.Index) -> A.Element` | `method descriptor for Swift.Collection.subscript(A.Index) -> A.Element.read` | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$s9RealityIO9AttributeC2atxSd_tcig` | `RealityIO.Attribute.subscript.getter : (at: Swift.Double) -> A` | `RealityIO.Attribute.subscript(at: Swift.Double) -> A.getter` | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$sSo13simd_float2x3a0A0Eys5SIMD3VySfGSiciM` | `(extension in simd):__C.simd_float2x3.subscript.modify : (Swift.Int) -> Swift.SIMD3<Swift.Float>` | `__C.simd_float2x3.subscript(Swift.Int) -> Swift.SIMD3<Swift.Float>.modify` | `__C.simd_float2x3.subscript.modify : (Swift.Int) -> Swift.SIMD3<Swift.Float>` |

In the last row `swift-demangle` also prints an `(extension in …)` prefix, which this demangler leaves out by design. That doesn't change here.

The fix:

- When a subscript has an accessor, it's printed as `subscript.<accessor> : <type>`, the same shape as a variable's accessor. A `static` subscript keeps `static` in front.

- Nothing else changes: which symbols decode, the rendering of the type and its argument labels, and the limits. Only the order of the parts in a subscript accessor is different.

  - `addressors_follow_subscript`: `unsafeAddressor` and `unsafeMutableAddressor` of `Swift.UnsafePointer` and `Swift.UnsafeMutablePointer`.
  - `accessors_inside_other_globals_follow_subscript`: a method descriptor, a dispatch thunk, a protocol witness and two `.resume.0` coroutine parts.
  - `static_subscript_accessors_follow_subscript`: two constructed with `swiftc -enable-library-evolution` (`static x.S.subscript.getter : (Swift.String) -> Swift.Int` and a `modify` with `.resume.0`).

With `main`'s `swift_demangle.rs`: `left: "Foundation.Data.InlineData.subscript(Swift.Int) -> Swift.UInt8.modify"`, `right: "Foundation.Data.InlineData.subscript.modify : (Swift.Int) -> Swift.UInt8"`. Of its 52 subscript symbols, 37 match `swift-demangle` here and 5 differ only in the `_:` label that #1453 adds (`subscript.getter : (_: Swift.String, default: Swift.Int) -> Swift.Int`). **Roadmap item:** R3.12, the new line "Swift value witness symbols decode…". It is claimed in its own commit and ticked in the fix.

**What changed:**

A symbol ending `w` and two letters is a value witness: one of the functions the Swift runtime calls to copy, move or destroy a value of a type, or to read and set the case of an enum value. The two letters say which one: `wxx` destroys a value, `wcp` copies it into fresh memory, `wug` reads an enum's case, and so on. `swift-demangle` prints the function's name, `value witness for` and the type, for example `destroy value witness for Foundation.Data`. `swift_demangle` had no `w` operator and reported every such symbol invalid ("unsupported operator 'w'"). They are about one symbol in twelve in the system binaries I compared.

Some symbols from macOS 15.7 and Xcode 26 system binaries:

| Symbol | `swift-demangle` | `main` | here |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_$s10Foundation4DataVwxx` | `destroy value witness for Foundation.Data` | invalid: unsupported operator 'w' | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$ss6ResultOwug` | `getEnumTag value witness for Swift.Result` | invalid: unsupported operator 'w' | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$sSD5IndexV8_VariantOwCP` | `initializeBufferWithCopyOfBuffer value witness for Swift.Dictionary.Index._Variant` | invalid: unsupported operator 'w' | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$s3SIL7OperandVwetTm` | `merged getEnumTagSinglePayload value witness for SIL.Operand` | invalid: unsupported operator 'w' | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$sSS7SWBUtilE7PadSideOwet` | `getEnumTagSinglePayload value witness for (extension in SWBUtil):Swift.String.PadSide` | invalid: unsupported operator 'w' | `getEnumTagSinglePayload value witness for Swift.String.PadSide` |

In the last row `swift-demangle` also prints an `(extension in …)` prefix, which this demangler leaves out by design. That doesn't change here.

The fix:

- A new `w` operator reads two letters and names the value witness. It knows the 24 codes `swift-demangle` accepts. I found them by giving `swift-demangle` `$s4main1AVw` followed by every pair of letters, digits and `_`. Any other pair is reported invalid ("unsupported value witness kind").
- The operand must be a whole type: a nominal type, a bound generic, an optional, a tuple, a function type, a generic parameter and so on. A module, a bare name, an extension, a member (such as a getter) or another global (such as `Ma` or `WV`) before `w` is reported invalid, as `swift-demangle` does.
- A merged value witness (`…wxxTm`) needs nothing new: the existing `Tm` rule adds `merged` in front.

With `main`'s `swift_demangle.rs`: every one stops at its first symbol with `_$s10Foundation4DataVwxx: Some("unsupported operator 'w'")` (`left: Invalid`, `right: Demangled`), and likewise for `_$ss6ResultOwug`, `_$s3SIL7OperandVwetTm`, `_$sSS7SWBUtilE7PadSideOwet` and `$s4main1AVwal`. - **Real symbols:** 2,361,216 distinct Swift symbols from `nm -j` on 4,113 Mach-O files of macOS 15.7.4 and Xcode 26.0 beta, compared with `swift-demangle` from the Command Line Tools (Swift 6.1.2). `main` here is `30e9165`.

  | Decoded, different text | 31,407 | 31,407 |

**Roadmap item:** R3.12, the new line "Swift symbols decode private declarations…". It is claimed in its own commit and ticked in the fix.

**What changed:**

A `private` or `fileprivate` declaration can share its name with a declaration in another file of the same module, so its symbol carries an identifier for the file that declares it: the declaration's name, then the file identifier (`_` and 32 hex digits, usually `33_<hash>`), then `LL`. `swift-demangle` prints the pair as `(name in _HASH)` wherever the name appears: a type, a protocol, a function, a variable, a nested type, a generic argument. `swift_demangle` read `L` as an unknown operator, so every symbol with a private name in it was reported invalid ("unsupported operator 'L'"). That is 326,718 of the 2,361,216 symbols in the corpus below; 139,551 of them decode now, and the rest stop at other manglings.

Some symbols from macOS 15.7 and Xcode 26 system binaries:

| Symbol | `swift-demangle` | `main` | here |

reviewed_pull_requests.body:
Refs #1438, #981 (not "fixes": see "Not verified").

## What was wrong

Every `Process` run has a time limit and a cancel, but when either fired (and after a normal exit, to clear leftovers) the supervisor called the process library's `kill()`. That call stops the program and then waits for it with no limit: for the process itself, and on Windows then for a job-object message the system doesn't promise to send. A program that outlives its stop held the supervisor thread, and so the run, for good. Nothing could reach it: the check's 90 s limit, the round's 30-minute limit and Pause all end in that same call.

That matches the reports: a check that sits for hours on Windows with Pause dead (#1438 at `app-screenshot`, past the 30-minute limit #1287 added).

## What changed

- `process::end`: stop the program, poll `try_wait` for 5 s (`REAP_GRACE`), log a warning and move on if it's still there. The supervisor uses it for all three cases (time limit, cancel, leftovers after exit).
- A regression test with a stand-in child that never goes away and whose `wait` never returns. It sits in `error_tests`, because `mod tests` in that file only builds on Unix.
- Roadmap line ticked, a follow-up line added, and a pitfalls entry.

## Verified

On Windows 11: `cargo test -p craft-anything-platform --no-fail-fast` (82 passed, 8 ignored, plus the integration tests), clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers | locks | secrets | wasm`, `cargo fmt --all --check`.

## Not verified

- The reporters' hangs are **not reproduced**. This was found by reading the code: it is the only wait without a limit on the path a check's program run takes. 1,200 short runs under 8 threads on Windows 11 never hung on `main`, so whatever triggers it is specific to their programs (all games).
- Not run on macOS or Linux here; CI covers Linux.
- `Launched::stop` (Play) and the console capture still call the unlimited `kill()`; left for the follow-up line rather than widening this change.

**Roadmap item:** R3.12, the new line "Swift arguments without a label read `_:` when another argument of the same function, initialiser or subscript has one". It is claimed in its own commit and ticked in the fix.

**What changed:**

A Swift function symbol carries the argument labels after the function's name: one identifier per argument, `_` for an argument without a label, or a single `y` when no argument has one. When at least one argument has a label, `swift-demangle` prints `_:` before each argument that has none, so `append(_:length:)` reads `append(_: Swift.UnsafeRawPointer, length: Swift.Int)`. `swift_demangle` printed the bare type for those arguments, so about 21,000 symbols differed from `swift-demangle` only in these labels. The same text shows inside protocol witnesses, dispatch thunks, method descriptors, merged functions, closures and default arguments, since they print the function they belong to.

Some symbols from macOS 15.7 and Xcode 26 system binaries:

| Symbol | `swift-demangle` | `main` | here |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_$s10Foundation13__DataStorageC6append_6lengthySV_SitF` | `Foundation.__DataStorage.append(_: Swift.UnsafeRawPointer, length: Swift.Int) -> ()` | `Foundation.__DataStorage.append(Swift.UnsafeRawPointer, length: Swift.Int) -> ()` | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$s4simd3mix__1ts5SIMD2VySdGAF_A2FtF` | `simd.mix(_: Swift.SIMD2<Swift.Double>, _: Swift.SIMD2<Swift.Double>, t: Swift.SIMD2<Swift.Double>) -> Swift.SIMD2<Swift.Double>` | `simd.mix(Swift.SIMD2<Swift.Double>, Swift.SIMD2<Swift.Double>, t: Swift.SIMD2<Swift.Double>) -> Swift.SIMD2<Swift.Double>` | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$s10PreviewsUI12DelayedValueC_9schedulerACyxq_Gx_q_tcfCTq` | `method descriptor for PreviewsUI.DelayedValue.__allocating_init(_: A, scheduler: B) -> PreviewsUI.DelayedValue<A, B>` | `method descriptor for PreviewsUI.DelayedValue.__allocating_init(A, scheduler: B) -> PreviewsUI.DelayedValue<A, B>` | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$s10Foundation4DataVSlAASl5index_8offsetBy5IndexQzAG_SitFTW` | `protocol witness for Swift.Collection.index(_: A.Index, offsetBy: Swift.Int) -> A.Index in conformance Foundation.Data : Swift.Collection in Foundation` | `protocol witness for Swift.Collection.index(A.Index, offsetBy: Swift.Int) -> A.Index in conformance Foundation.Data : Swift.Collection in Foundation` | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$s10Foundation10URLRequestV13XcodeCloudKitE_7baseURLAC14OpenAPIRuntime7RequestV_AA0G0VtKcfC` | `(extension in XcodeCloudKit):Foundation.URLRequest.init(_: OpenAPIRuntime.Request, baseURL: Foundation.URL) throws -> Foundation.URLRequest` | `Foundation.URLRequest.init(OpenAPIRuntime.Request, baseURL: Foundation.URL) throws -> Foundation.URLRequest` | `Foundation.URLRequest.init(_: OpenAPIRuntime.Request, baseURL: Foundation.URL) throws -> Foundation.URLRequest` |

The rule, worked out from `swift-demangle`'s output on the corpus and on constructed symbols:

- If at least one argument has a label, every argument without one reads `_:`, wherever it stands (first, middle, last, several in a row) and whatever its type (`inout`, a tuple, a function, a generic parameter, a metatype).

- Subscripts follow the same rule (`main.T.subscript.getter : (i: Swift.Int, _: Swift.String) -> Swift.Int`). An enum case symbol (`WC`) prints its payload as a function type with no labels, and that stays as it was.

The fix:

- `params_text` prints `_:` for an argument without a label when the entity has at least one label, and prints a single argument that isn't a tuple without its label.
- Nothing else changes: which symbols decode, the label list parsing and the limits. Tuple types outside an argument list print as before.
- Docs: a Swift argument labels row in STATUS.md, and the roadmap line under R3.12.

- **New test:** `crates/formats/tests/swift_demangle_unlabeled_args.rs`, five tests.

  - `a_label_list_that_does_not_fit_the_arguments_is_invalid`: four constructed symbols with too few or too many labels, which `swift-demangle` rejects.
  - Four of the five fail on `main` and pass here. With `main`'s `swift_demangle.rs`: `left: "Foundation.__DataStorage.append(Swift.UnsafeRawPointer, length: Swift.Int) -> ()"`, `right: "Foundation.__DataStorage.append(_: Swift.UnsafeRawPointer, length: Swift.Int) -> ()"`; the bare-arguments test fails on the constructed `main.S.one(a: Swift.Int) -> ()`. The invalid-symbols test passes on `main` as well; it guards that the label count check stays as it was.
- **Real symbols:** 2,361,216 distinct Swift symbols from `nm -j` on 4,113 Mach-O files of macOS 15.7.4 and Xcode 26.0 beta, compared with `swift-demangle` from the Command Line Tools (Swift 6.1.2). `main` here is `30e9165`.

  | Differs only in the `(extension in …)` prefix | 41,844 | 43,340 |
  | Decoded, different text | 31,407 | 10,066 |
  | Reported invalid | 1,137,501 | 1,137,501 |
  | Rejected by `swift-demangle` too | 2,574 | 2,574 |

reviewed_pull_requests.body:
**Roadmap item:** R3.12, the new line "Swift symbols name the type metadata singleton initialization cache…". It is claimed in its own commit and ticked in the fix.

**What changed:**

A symbol ending `Ml` is the cache the Swift runtime fills the first time it lays out the metadata of a type whose layout is only known at run time (for example a struct holding a field from another resilient module). `swift-demangle` prints it as `type metadata singleton initialization cache for` and the type. A symbol ending `ML` is a different global, the lazy cache variable for a type's metadata. `swift_demangle` gave both letters the `ML` name, so every `Ml` symbol decoded with the wrong text.

Some symbols from macOS 15.7 and Xcode 26 system binaries:

| Symbol | `swift-demangle` | `main` | here |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_$ss20__BridgingHashBufferCMl` | `type metadata singleton initialization cache for Swift.__BridgingHashBuffer` | `lazy cache variable for type metadata for Swift.__BridgingHashBuffer` | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$s10RealityKit21BodyTrackingComponentVMl` | `type metadata singleton initialization cache for RealityKit.BodyTrackingComponent` | `lazy cache variable for type metadata for RealityKit.BodyTrackingComponent` | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$s10RealityKit15TextureResourceC9LoadErrorOMl` | `type metadata singleton initialization cache for RealityKit.TextureResource.LoadError` | `lazy cache variable for type metadata for RealityKit.TextureResource.LoadError` | same as `swift-demangle` |
| `_$s10RealityKit18AnchoringComponentV0A10FoundationE05ImageC6SourceV0G0OMl` | `type metadata singleton initialization cache for (extension in RealityFoundation):RealityKit.AnchoringComponent.ImageAnchoringSource.Source` | `lazy cache variable for type metadata for RealityKit.AnchoringComponent.ImageAnchoringSource.Source` | `type metadata singleton initialization cache for RealityKit.AnchoringComponent.ImageAnchoringSource.Source` |

In the last row `swift-demangle` also prints an `(extension in …)` prefix, which this demangler leaves out by design. That doesn't change here.

The fix:

- In the table of metadata kinds after `M`, `l` now has its own name, `type metadata singleton initialization cache for`. `L` keeps `lazy cache variable for type metadata for`.
- Nothing else changes: which symbols decode, the rendering of the type, and the limits. Only the prefix text of `Ml` symbols is different.
- Docs: a Swift metadata caches row in STATUS.md, and the roadmap line under R3.12.

**Verified:**

- **New test:** `crates/formats/tests/swift_demangle_singleton_cache.rs`, five tests.
  - `ml_reads_as_the_singleton_initialization_cache`: a class, a struct and an enum from system binaries.
  - `ml_after_a_nested_type_reads_as_the_singleton_initialization_cache`: two real nested types and one constructed with `swiftc -enable-library-evolution` (`main.Outer.Inner`).
  - `ml_after_a_type_in_an_extension_leaves_out_the_extension_prefix`: the `RealityKit` symbol above and a constructed type declared in an extension of `Swift.Int`.
  - `capital_ml_still_reads_as_the_lazy_cache_variable`: two real `ML` symbols (`Foundation.URL?` and `(Foundation.URL, Foundation.URL)?`).
  - `ml_without_a_whole_type_is_invalid`: three constructed symbols that `swift-demangle` rejects (`$sMl`, `$s4main1AVMl1`, `$s4main1AVM`).
  - Three of the five fail on `main` and pass here. With `main`'s `swift_demangle.rs`: `left: "lazy cache variable for type metadata for Swift.__BridgingHashBuffer"`, `right: "type metadata singleton initialization cache for Swift.__BridgingHashBuffer"`. The `ML` test and the invalid-symbols test pass on `main` as well; they guard that `ML` and the error paths stay as they were.
- **Real symbols:** 2,361,216 distinct Swift symbols from `nm -j` on 4,113 Mach-O files of macOS 15.7.4 and Xcode 26.0 beta, compared with `swift-demangle` from the Command Line Tools (Swift 6.1.2). `main` here is `30e9165`.

  | | `main` | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | Same text as `swift-demangle` | 1,147,890 | 1,153,191 |
  | Differs only in the `(extension in …)` prefix | 41,844 | 41,877 |
  | Decoded, different text | 31,407 | 26,073 |
  | Reported invalid | 1,137,501 | 1,137,501 |
  | Rejected by `swift-demangle` too | 2,574 | 2,574 |

  The corpus has 6,000 symbols ending `Ml`. They are the only symbols that changed: 5,334 outputs, all decoded on `main` with the `ML` name.
  - 5,301 now match `swift-demangle` exactly.
  - 33 differ only in the `(extension in …)` prefix.
  - The other 666 were reported invalid on `main` and still are, for other manglings: 662 private discriminators (`…LL`, "unsupported operator 'L'"), 2 local types inside functions (`…L_VMl`, `…L_CMl`) whose signatures use other unsupported manglings, and 2 malformed symbols that `swift-demangle` rejects too.
  - No symbol that matched before changed, and none of the 4,494 `ML` symbols changed.
- **Constructed symbols:** I compiled a struct, an enum, a class with an imported superclass, a nested struct and a struct in an extension, each holding a `Foundation.URL`, with `swiftc -enable-library-evolution`. All five `Ml` symbols and the one `ML` symbol match `swift-demangle` here, except the extension prefix.
- **Checks**, run on macOS arm64 with Rust 1.99.1, all green:
  - `cargo test -p craft-anything-formats`: 1,078 passed;
  - `cargo clippy -p craft-anything-formats --all-targets -- -D warnings`;
  - `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask locks`, `cargo xtask secrets`, `cargo xtask wasm`.

**Not verified:**

- No `Ml` symbol of a generic type is in the corpus, and the generic types I compiled get other caches, so a generic type before `Ml` is untested.
- A module or another global before `Ml` (`$s4mainMl`, `$s4main1AVMaMl`) decodes here and `swift-demangle` rejects it. That was already so on `main` for every metadata kind (`$s4mainML` and `$s4main1AVMaMa` decode too), and no real symbol has this shape. I left it alone.
- All symbols compared use the `$s` mangling. `$S`, `_T0` and `$e` are not compared.
- I didn't run `apple_swift_symbols_demangle` through the engine or the CLI. The module was called directly.

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p <crates> --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
      `cargo test -p <crates>`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask secrets`
- [x] Docs in this PR: the roadmap line ticked (and new `- [ ]` lines for what's left), STATUS if
      what works changed, `cargo xtask tools` if tools were added
- [x] No other tool's code, scripts or wording copied (behaviour only; AGENTS.md)

## Changes

Apply the reviewed test-suite cleanup: remove tests that only check their own fixtures, fold duplicate cases into tables, retain distinct input/output guarantees, and make kept regression tests exercise production behavior. The review changes include mutation proofs recorded in the lane reports.

### Production fixes

1. Transcript capture advances past refused or unavailable handoffs; recovery and restart cannot replay outage-window inference inputs, while fresh input still works.
2. Cowork drops failed inference inputs and retires legacy inference spool entries; metadata delivery remains separate.
3. OpenCode no longer retries refused capture POSTs in the background.

5. CCS Align refuses corrupt exclusion state without re-admitting excluded observations or overwriting the corrupt file.
6. The viewer recognizes `sensitive` observations, with its expected types derived from shipped mode definitions.

Phase R restores Cowork's normal 8-second remote HTTPS timeout under the existing hook budget, adds delayed-response regressions, removes the inert transcript checkpoint gate and its exclusive accessors, and removes stale wrapper documentation. ### CI and test lanes
